newsitem.title: UK: UK utilities face possible tax threat - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK utilities face possible tax threat - paper.

text.p: Privatised British utilities face the threat of a new tax which could cost them more than three billion sterling a year, whoever wins the election, a British newspaper said.
The Observer said a government committee was investigating changes to the way rates are levied on the electricity, water, gas and rail industries.

Currently they pay rates according to an arbitrary formula set when they were still publicly owned, the report said, but the Wood Committee set up by the Department of the Environment is considering linking the rates to profits.
Industry analysts said the change could raise annual business rates bills for the utilities to over 4.5 billion sterling from a current one billion.
The Wood Committee is due to report on September.
